reason: Rs 5,000 with money back if it can't price 7 in 10 quotes off my own Excel is a small bet, and quoting by hand eats my evenings every time rates move. I'll try the pilot, but I'm not promising the Rs 60,000 until I see it work on my real enquiries.
objection: Rs 60,000 plus Rs 5,000 every month is a lot for what is still a WhatsApp-and-Excel tool, and my rates change all the time, so I doubt it keeps up. Also, who looks after it if this small studio closes? The handover in writing helps, but who will actually run the code then?
would_change_my_mind: If the pilot quotes come out wrong when raw material rates change mid-week, or the reference call with the chemical trader is weak, I stop after the pilot. If they come out right, I'll still push for the Rs 45,000 founding price or lower before I pay for setup.
